description: Personalize a future learning plan by first understanding how the user learns best and what limits them.

title: Weekly Study Plan Generator
description: Turn a broader roadmap into a specific weekly schedule.
prompt: Based on my goal of [GOAL] in [SKILL] and [TIME AVAILABLE PER DAY] available, create a weekly study plan that allocates time across learning fundamentals, deliberate practice, and applied projects, in a realistic and sustainable ratio.

title: Progressive Difficulty Curriculum
description: Sequence learning content so difficulty increases at a sustainable pace.
prompt: Design a progressive-difficulty curriculum for [SKILL] that starts at [CURRENT LEVEL] and gradually increases challenge level, avoiding both boredom (too easy) and overwhelm (too hard) at each stage. Explain how to know when I'm ready to advance to harder material.

title: Limited-Resource Learning Plan
description: Design an effective learning plan when the user has limited access to tools, money, or materials.
prompt: Design a learning plan for [SKILL] assuming I only have access to these resources: [RESOURCES]. Prioritize free or low-cost methods and be resourceful about how I can still practice deliberately and get feedback despite the limitations.

title: Tight Deadline Learning Sprint
description: Design an intensive plan for someone who needs to reach a usable level of a skill fast.
prompt: I need to become functionally competent at [SKILL] by [DEADLINE], which is a tight timeline. Design an intensive sprint plan that focuses only on the 20% of the skill that delivers 80% of practical value for my specific goal of [GOAL], cutting anything non-essential.

title: Interleaved Practice Schedule
description: Design a study plan that mixes related subskills instead of practicing one thing at a time in isolation.
prompt: Design an interleaved practice schedule for [SKILL] that mixes these subskills: [list subskills], rather than mastering one at a time in isolation. Explain the mixing pattern and why it improves retention and transfer compared to blocked practice.

title: Learning Plan Adjustment Check-In
description: Revise an existing learning plan based on real progress and obstacles encountered so far.
prompt: Here is my current learning plan for [SKILL]: [paste plan]. Here's what's actually happened over the past [time period]: [describe progress/obstacles]. Revise the plan to reflect reality, adjusting pacing, priorities, or methods as needed.

title: Fundamentals-First Explainer
description: Ensure a learner truly understands the core fundamentals before moving to advanced material.
prompt: Explain the true fundamentals of [SKILL] — the small number of core principles that everything else builds on. For each one, check my understanding by asking me to explain it back in my own words before moving to the next.

title: Difficult Concept Breakdown
description: Break down one specific concept a learner is struggling with into an understandable explanation.
prompt: I'm struggling to understand [specific concept] within [SKILL]. Ask me what specifically confuses me about it, then explain it using a different approach (analogy, example, or breakdown) than however it's normally taught, tailored to where my confusion is.

title: Analogy Generator for Abstract Concepts
description: Make an abstract or technical concept concrete using a relatable analogy.
prompt: Explain [specific concept] in [SKILL] using an analogy from an everyday domain I'm already familiar with. Then explain where the analogy breaks down, so I don't over-rely on it.

title: Concept Map Builder
description: Visualize how the key concepts in a skill relate to and depend on each other.
prompt: Create a text-based concept map for [SKILL], showing how the key concepts and subskills relate to and depend on one another. Highlight which concepts are true prerequisites for others.

title: Common Beginner Misconceptions Audit
description: Identify and correct the misconceptions most beginners have about a skill.
prompt: List the most common misconceptions beginners have when learning [SKILL], explain why each one is wrong, and ask me a few questions to check whether I currently hold any of them.

title: Explain-It-Simply Test
description: Test true understanding by requiring the learner to explain a concept as simply as possible.
prompt: Ask me to explain [specific concept] in [SKILL] as if to a complete beginner, in plain language with no jargon. Evaluate my explanation for gaps, and point out anything I glossed over that suggests I don't fully understand it yet.

title: Deliberate Practice Session Designer
description: Design a focused practice session targeting a specific weak point rather than general practice.
prompt: Design a 30-minute deliberate practice session for [SKILL] that targets specifically [WEAKNESS], not general practice. Include a warm-up, the focused practice task, and a way to self-evaluate immediately afterward.

title: Repetition Drill Generator
description: Generate a structured set of repetition drills for a specific subskill.
prompt: Create a set of 5 progressively harder repetition drills for practicing [specific subskill] within [SKILL], suitable for someone at [CURRENT LEVEL]. Each drill should build on the previous one.

title: Micro-Skill Isolation Practice
description: Isolate one small component of a larger skill to practice it in focused repetition.
prompt: Take this larger skill or task: [describe task] within [SKILL], and break out one small micro-skill within it that I can isolate and drill repeatedly until it becomes automatic. Design a short, repeatable isolation exercise for it.

title: Constraint-Based Practice Challenge
description: Add an artificial constraint to practice to force deeper skill development.
prompt: Give me a practice challenge in [SKILL] with an artificial constraint (time limit, limited resources, no reference material, etc.) that will force me to develop the skill more deeply than practicing without constraints.

title: Speed & Accuracy Training Plan
description: Design practice specifically aimed at improving speed without sacrificing accuracy.
prompt: Design a training plan to improve my speed at [specific task] within [SKILL] without sacrificing accuracy. Include how to measure both, and a method for gradually increasing speed demands.

title: Practice Session Self-Debrief
description: Structure a short reflection immediately after a practice session to lock in learning.
prompt: After a practice session on [SKILL], ask me a short set of debrief questions covering what went well, what felt hard, what I'd do differently, and one specific thing to focus on next time.

title: Daily Micro-Practice Habit Design
description: Design a very small, sustainable daily practice habit that's hard to skip.
prompt: Design a daily micro-practice habit for [SKILL] that takes no more than 10-15 minutes, is specific enough that I can't talk myself out of it, and compounds over time toward [GOAL].

title: Active Recall Quiz Generator
description: Generate quiz questions that test recall rather than recognition.
prompt: Create a 10-question active recall quiz on [SKILL] (or specifically on [specific topic]) at a difficulty appropriate for [CURRENT LEVEL]. Questions should require me to actively recall and apply information, not just recognize it from multiple choice.

title: Spaced Repetition Review Schedule
description: Design a spaced review schedule for key concepts to prevent forgetting.
prompt: Based on these key concepts I've recently learned in [SKILL]: [list concepts], design a spaced repetition review schedule over the next 30 days, telling me exactly when to review each one.

title: Recall-Before-Reveal Study Session
description: Force retrieval practice by requiring an attempt before showing the answer.
prompt: Quiz me on [specific topic] within [SKILL] one question at a time. After each question, wait for my answer before revealing anything — do not show the correct answer or explanation until I've responded.

title: Teach-It-Back Retention Check
description: Test retention by having the user teach a concept back without notes.
prompt: Ask me to teach you [specific concept] in [SKILL] from memory, without looking anything up. Play the role of a curious student and ask follow-up questions that expose any gaps in my understanding.

title: Forgetting Curve Diagnostic
description: Identify which previously learned concepts are at risk of being forgotten.
prompt: Here's a list of concepts I learned over the past [time period] in [SKILL]: [list concepts]. Ask me to recall each one from memory, then flag which ones show signs of fading and need review soon.

title: Detailed Work Critique
description: Get a structured, specific critique of a piece of work in the target skill.
prompt: Act as an expert in [SKILL]. Critique this piece of my work: [paste work]. Structure your feedback into what's working, what's not, and the single highest-leverage improvement I should make next, with specific reasoning.

title: Mistake Pattern Analysis
description: Identify recurring patterns across multiple pieces of work rather than one-off mistakes.
prompt: Here are several pieces of my recent work in [SKILL]: [paste multiple examples]. Identify recurring mistake patterns across them (not one-off errors), and explain the likely root cause behind the pattern.

title: Corrective Guidance After a Mistake
description: Turn a specific mistake into a clear, actionable correction.
prompt: I made this mistake while practicing [SKILL]: [describe mistake]. Explain specifically why it happened, what the correct approach is, and give me one practice exercise to fix it.

title: Harsh-to-Constructive Feedback Reframe
description: Get honest, high-standard feedback delivered in a constructive way.
prompt: Give me honest, high-standard feedback on this [SKILL] work as a demanding expert would: [paste work]. Be direct about weaknesses, but frame everything constructively with a clear path to improvement, not just criticism.

title: Weakness-Targeted Practice Assignment
description: Turn an identified weakness directly into a specific practice assignment.
prompt: My identified weakness in [SKILL] is [WEAKNESS]. Design a specific, targeted practice assignment aimed directly at fixing this weakness, along with a way to measure whether it's improving.

title: Peer-Review Simulation
description: Simulate the kind of feedback a skilled peer or reviewer would give.
prompt: Review this [SKILL] work as a skilled peer reviewer would — not overly harsh, not overly nice, just realistic and specific: [paste work]. Include at least one thing I clearly did well and one clear area to improve.

title: Rubric-Based Self-Evaluation
description: Give the user a rubric so they can evaluate their own work objectively.
prompt: Create a simple rubric (4-5 criteria, each rated 1-5) for evaluating work in [SKILL] at [CURRENT LEVEL]. Then help me apply it to this piece of my own work: [paste work], and identify where the rubric reveals a gap I hadn't noticed.

title: Plateau Diagnosis & Breakthrough Plan
description: Diagnose why progress has stalled and create a plan to break through it.
prompt: I've plateaued in [SKILL] — my progress has stalled despite continuing to practice. Ask me about my current practice routine, then diagnose the most likely reason for the plateau and design a specific plan to break through it.

title: Procrastination Root-Cause Interview
description: Identify the real reason a learner keeps avoiding practice, rather than assuming laziness.
prompt: I keep procrastinating on practicing [SKILL]. Ask me questions to identify the real underlying reason (fear of failure, unclear next step, boredom, overwhelm, etc.), then suggest a specific fix targeted at that actual cause.

title: Motivation Recovery After a Break
description: Help a learner who has fallen off their practice routine get back on track without guilt.
prompt: I haven't practiced [SKILL] in [time period] and lost momentum. Help me get back into it without dwelling on guilt — assess where I likely still stand skill-wise, and suggest a low-pressure re-entry plan for this week.

title: Consistency System Design
description: Build a system that makes consistent practice more likely regardless of daily motivation.
prompt: Design a consistency system for practicing [SKILL] that doesn't rely on daily motivation — include triggers, environment design, and a way to track streaks, so I keep practicing even on low-motivation days.

title: Boredom & Plateau Variety Injection
description: Introduce variety into practice to reignite engagement without abandoning the plan.
prompt: My practice routine for [SKILL] has become boring and I'm losing engagement. Suggest 5 ways to add variety to my practice without abandoning my overall learning plan or losing progress toward [GOAL].

title: Accountability Check-In System
description: Simulate a recurring accountability partner to keep the learner on track.
prompt: Act as my accountability partner for learning [SKILL]. At the start of each conversation, ask me what I committed to since we last talked, whether I followed through, and if not, what got in the way — without judgment, just honest tracking.

title: Progressive Challenge Generator
description: Generate a series of challenges that increase in difficulty as competence improves.
prompt: Give me a problem or challenge in [SKILL] appropriate for [CURRENT LEVEL]. After I respond, evaluate my solution, then give me a slightly harder challenge that builds on what I just did. Repeat this pattern.

title: Real-World Scenario Simulation
description: Simulate a realistic scenario the learner might face when applying the skill in practice.
prompt: Simulate a realistic scenario I might face when applying [SKILL] in [context, e.g., a real job, a real project]. Walk me through it step by step, asking me what I'd do at each decision point, and give feedback on my choices.

title: Debugging & Troubleshooting Practice
description: Practice diagnosing and fixing a deliberately broken example.
prompt: Give me a deliberately flawed example of [SKILL] output (with a mistake embedded) and ask me to identify what's wrong and how to fix it before revealing the actual issue.

title: Constraint-Based Problem Set
description: Solve realistic problems under limitations to build practical adaptability.
prompt: Give me 3 problems in [SKILL] that each come with a specific real-world constraint (limited time, limited tools, limited information). Evaluate my solutions with attention to how well I worked within the constraint.

title: Multiple-Approach Comparison Exercise
description: Practice generating and comparing multiple solutions instead of settling for the first one.
prompt: Give me a problem in [SKILL] and ask me to generate at least two different valid approaches to solving it before picking one. Then help me compare the tradeoffs between my approaches.

title: Applied Project Brief Generator
description: Turn skill practice into a small, realistic project rather than isolated exercises.
prompt: Design a small, realistic project brief in [SKILL] appropriate for [CURRENT LEVEL] that would take about [time estimate] to complete, and would meaningfully apply what I've learned so far toward [GOAL].

title: Performance Test Simulation
description: Simulate the actual conditions of a real test, interview, or performance situation.
prompt: Simulate a realistic [test/interview/performance] situation for [SKILL] as close to the real thing as possible, including time pressure and realistic difficulty. Afterward, give me honest feedback on how I'd likely perform in the real situation.

title: Job-Readiness Assessment
description: Assess whether a learner's current skill level is sufficient for a specific job or role requirement.
prompt: Based on my current ability in [SKILL] (described here: [CURRENT LEVEL]), assess whether I'm ready to apply my skill in a real [job/role] context. Identify the specific gaps between where I am and what's typically expected.

title: Under-Pressure Practice Simulation
description: Practice performing the skill under realistic pressure or stress conditions.
prompt: Give me a practice task in [SKILL] under simulated pressure (tight time limit, unexpected complication, or high stakes framing) so I can build comfort performing under stress, not just in ideal conditions.

title: Mock Evaluation Panel
description: Simulate feedback from multiple different perspectives, as a real evaluation panel might give.
prompt: Act as a panel of 3 different evaluators judging my [SKILL] work: [paste work] — one focused on technical quality, one on practical usefulness, and one on presentation/communication. Give me each perspective separately.

title: Client or Stakeholder Simulation
description: Practice applying the skill in response to a realistic client or stakeholder request.
prompt: Simulate a realistic client or stakeholder request involving [SKILL], including the kind of vague or conflicting requirements that happen in real situations. Respond to my proposed solution the way a real client might, including follow-up questions or pushback.

title: Exemplary Work Breakdown
description: Analyze a piece of expert-level work to extract specific, transferable lessons.
prompt: Analyze this example of expert-level [SKILL] work: [paste or describe example]. Break down specifically what makes it excellent, in terms I can apply to my own practice, not just general praise.

title: Expert Mindset Interview Simulation
description: Simulate a conversation with an expert to understand how they actually think about the skill.
prompt: Act as a world-class expert in [SKILL]. I'll ask you questions about how you approach [specific aspect of the skill], and I want you to answer the way a real expert would — including the intuitions and heuristics that don't usually make it into textbooks.

title: Before/After Comparison Analysis
description: Compare a beginner-level and expert-level version of the same task to isolate what actually changes with skill.
prompt: Compare a beginner-level and an expert-level approach to this task in [SKILL]: [describe task]. Show me specifically what changes between the two, not just that one is 'better'.

title: Style/Technique Extraction from a Model
description: Extract a reusable technique or pattern from a specific piece of exemplary work.
prompt: Look at this example of skilled [SKILL] work: [paste example]. Extract one specific, reusable technique or pattern I could practice applying to my own work.

title: Progress Tracking Dashboard Design
description: Design a simple system for tracking measurable progress over time.
prompt: Design a simple progress-tracking system for learning [SKILL] toward [GOAL], including what specific metrics to track (not just 'time spent'), and how often to review them.

title: Competence Testing Checkpoint
description: Test whether a learner has genuinely reached a target competence level.
prompt: Give me a realistic test to check whether I've genuinely reached [GOAL] in [SKILL], not just whether I've completed a curriculum. Evaluate my result honestly against what true competence at this level looks like.

title: Milestone Review & Reflection
description: Structure a periodic review of progress against the original learning roadmap.
prompt: I'm at the [milestone] point in my learning roadmap for [SKILL]. Review my progress against the original plan, ask me reflection questions about what's working and what isn't, and adjust my next milestone if needed.

title: Before-and-After Skill Comparison
description: Compare current work against an earlier baseline to make invisible progress visible.
prompt: Here's my baseline work in [SKILL] from [time period ago]: [paste old example]. Here's my current work: [paste recent example]. Compare them specifically and tell me exactly what has improved and what hasn't yet.

title: Readiness-for-Next-Level Check
description: Determine whether a learner is actually ready to move to more advanced material.
prompt: Based on this description of my current ability in [SKILL]: [describe ability], assess honestly whether I'm ready to move to more advanced material, or whether I should consolidate at my current level first, and why.

title: Portfolio Piece Selection & Polish
description: Identify which work is portfolio-worthy and how to polish it further.
prompt: Here's a collection of my work in [SKILL]: [describe or list pieces]. Help me identify which pieces are strong enough to include in a portfolio for [GOAL], and what specific polish each one still needs.

title: Teach-the-Skill Lesson Plan
description: Have the learner design a lesson to teach the skill, reinforcing their own mastery.
prompt: Help me design a short lesson to teach [specific concept] in [SKILL] to a complete beginner. Creating this lesson should force me to organize and solidify my own understanding — point out anywhere my explanation reveals a gap.

title: Advanced Nuance & Edge Case Exploration
description: Push a competent learner into the nuanced, edge-case understanding that separates advanced practitioners.
prompt: I'm already competent at [SKILL] and want to reach an advanced level. Challenge me with nuanced edge cases, exceptions, or advanced scenarios that most intermediate practitioners haven't encountered yet, and evaluate how I handle them.

title: Signature Style Development
description: Help an advancing learner move from correct execution to a distinctive, personal approach.
prompt: I can execute [SKILL] competently but want to develop a more distinctive personal style or approach. Ask me about my values, preferences, and strengths within the skill, then suggest directions I could develop that would feel authentically mine rather than generic.

title: Long-Term Mastery Maintenance Plan
description: Design a sustainable plan to maintain and continue improving a skill after reaching competence.
prompt: I've reached a solid level of competence in [SKILL]. Design a long-term maintenance plan that keeps my skill sharp and continues gradual improvement, without requiring the intensity of my original learning phase.

title: Complete Personalized Learning System
description: A comprehensive master prompt combining assessment, roadmap, and practice into one adaptive system.
prompt: Act as a complete personalized learning system for [SKILL]. First, interview me about my current level, goal ([GOAL]), deadline ([DEADLINE]), time available ([TIME AVAILABLE PER DAY]), and learning style. Then build me a full roadmap with phases, and for each phase, generate practice tasks, quiz me with active recall, give feedback on my attempts, and adjust the plan based on how I'm actually performing.

title: Adaptive Skill Coach
description: An ongoing coaching system that adjusts difficulty and focus based on real-time performance.
prompt: Act as my ongoing adaptive coach for [SKILL]. Each session, give me one practice task calibrated to my recent performance, evaluate my result, identify the specific weakness it reveals, and use that to decide the next task — increasing difficulty as I improve and revisiting weak areas as needed.

title: 30-Day Skill Sprint System
description: A complete intensive 30-day program combining planning, daily practice, and review.
prompt: Design a complete 30-day sprint system to build functional competence in [SKILL] toward [GOAL]. Include a week-by-week structure, daily practice tasks, a mid-sprint checkpoint to adjust based on progress, and a final assessment on day 30.

title: 90-Day Mastery Roadmap System
description: A longer-term structured system moving a learner from competence toward advanced mastery.
prompt: Design a complete 90-day mastery roadmap for [SKILL], moving me from [CURRENT LEVEL] toward [GOAL]. Structure it into three 30-day phases with distinct focuses, milestones at the end of each phase, and a way to test readiness before advancing to the next phase.

title: Deliberate Practice Engine
description: A repeatable system that keeps generating targeted deliberate practice based on identified weaknesses.
prompt: Act as a deliberate practice engine for [SKILL]. Each time I tell you what I just practiced and how it went, identify the specific weakness revealed, generate a new focused practice task targeting exactly that weakness, and repeat this cycle continuously.

title: Weakness-Detection System
description: A system that continuously scans the learner's work for recurring weaknesses across sessions.
prompt: Act as a weakness-detection system for my ongoing [SKILL] practice. Each time I share new work or practice results, compare it against patterns from my previous submissions (which I'll keep sharing), and flag any weakness that keeps recurring across sessions rather than treating each submission in isolation.

title: Real-World Simulation Coach
description: A system that repeatedly simulates realistic application scenarios and coaches through them.
prompt: Act as a real-world simulation coach for [SKILL]. Repeatedly present me with realistic scenarios I might face in [context], let me respond, then coach me through what worked and what didn't, gradually increasing the realism and difficulty of scenarios as I improve.

title: Complete Skill Assessment System
description: A thorough, multi-part assessment that produces a full picture of current ability.
prompt: Act as a complete skill assessment system for [SKILL]. Combine diagnostic questions, a practical test task, and a self-rating comparison to produce a full, honest picture of my current ability across all major subskills, along with a prioritized list of what to work on first.

title: Auto-Escalating Progression System
description: A system that automatically increases challenge difficulty as the learner demonstrates improvement.
prompt: Act as an auto-escalating progression system for [SKILL]. Start me at a challenge level appropriate for [CURRENT LEVEL]. After each attempt, evaluate my performance and automatically increase the difficulty of the next challenge if I succeed, or provide a supporting exercise if I struggle, without me having to ask.
